properties.name: `incoming` exists on every relation link and no served skill mentions it, so a reporter drew two edges backwards and then filed the flag as missing
properties.statement: FLO2 F16 was filed claiming `review_relations` can only draw edges FROM its own node, and CORRECTED the same day by its own author: the `incoming` flag exists and works. MEASURED 2026-09-19: `incoming` is in review_relations' published schema, and `grep` over all 30 served skills finds the word in NONE of them. The cost was paid twice before the correction — two BLOCKS edges landed asserting the reverse of what their own `evidence` prose said, caught only by the reporter re-reading their own call — and then a third time in work: believing no flag existed, they routed two relations through create_edge by hand and wrote a script to verify direction. ⭐ THE SHAPE, and the reporter names it as the fifth instance in one file: the field existed, the tool served it, and its absence was inferred from a reply and from a skill that did not mention it. 'An API is not a schema — and a skill is not an API reference either.' This is the three-legs rule with the INSTRUCTION leg missing: the brainstorm skill's step 4 tells an agent that direction is part of the claim and that nothing will catch a reversal, and then does not name the remedy the tool already offers.
